criteria.expected: The configured board is ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1 and the target MCU is ESP32-C3.

criteria.criterion: A successful DHT22 read produces a temperature measurement.
criteria.observable: The temperature result returned or reported by the DHT22 read path
preconditions: A DHT22 is connected to the configured data pin and is able to provide a valid measurement.
procedure: Run the firmware with the connected DHT22.
Request a DHT22 measurement.
Inspect the temperature result.
criteria.expected: The read path produces a numeric temperature measurement rather than a read failure or an absent value.

preconditions: A DHT22 is connected to the configured data pin and is able to provide a valid measurement.

criteria.criterion: The MPU6050 measurement output reports numeric acceleration values for all three axes with m/s² units.
criteria.observable: The reported MPU6050 acceleration fields and their unit labels
preconditions: An MPU6050 is connected and initialized.
procedure: Run the firmware with the connected MPU6050.
Acquire and report an acceleration measurement.
Inspect the reported X, Y, and Z acceleration fields and units.
criteria.expected: Numeric X, Y, and Z acceleration values are reported, and each is identified in m/s².

criteria.criterion: The orientation calculation returns gyroscope-derived angle values represented in degrees.
criteria.observable: The orientation calculation's angle outputs and unit representation
preconditions: The orientation calculation can be called with supplied gyroscope samples or fake sensor I/O.
procedure: Call the orientation calculation with a gyroscope sample sequence that produces a nonzero orientation change.
Inspect the calculated angle outputs and their unit representation.
criteria.expected: The calculation produces numeric orientation angle values, and those values are represented in degrees.

criteria.criterion: With the same simulated motion sequence, accelerometer-assisted tilt correction yields a smaller tilt error than gyroscope-only integration.
criteria.observable: The corrected and gyroscope-only tilt estimates compared with the simulated reference tilt
preconditions: The orientation logic can be called with injected gyroscope and accelerometer samples.
The simulated sequence includes a known tilt reference and conditions under which accelerometer correction applies.
procedure: Feed the same simulated sequence to the accelerometer-assisted orientation calculation and a gyroscope-only baseline.
Compare each resulting tilt estimate with the simulated reference tilt.
criteria.expected: The absolute tilt error of the accelerometer-assisted estimate is lower than the absolute tilt error of the gyroscope-only estimate.
criteria.rationale: The acceptance criterion says accelerometer-assisted correction is used to reduce drift in applicable orientation axes. Comparing tilt error against a gyroscope-only baseline checks that the correction reduces drift without assuming a particular filter, parameter value, or numerical threshold.

criteria.criterion: A failed sensor read does not terminate the measurement loop, which performs a subsequent measurement-loop iteration.
criteria.observable: The measurement-loop iteration count or a subsequent iteration's mock sensor-read call
preconditions: The measurement loop can be exercised with fake sensor I/O.
A fake sensor read is configured to fail on one iteration.
procedure: Start the measurement loop with the fake sensor read configured to fail.
Allow the failed read to occur.
Check that the loop reaches a later iteration.
criteria.expected: At least one measurement-loop iteration occurs after the failed sensor read.

criteria.criterion: The orientation update does not use accelerometer-derived correction to establish yaw, and its yaw state remains capable of changing through gyroscope integration.
criteria.observable: The yaw update and accelerometer-correction terms in the orientation algorithm
procedure: Inspect the orientation algorithm's yaw update.
Trace whether accelerometer-derived correction is applied to yaw.
Check whether gyroscope integration can change the yaw state over time.
criteria.expected: No accelerometer-derived correction establishes an absolute yaw reference, and gyroscope integration can cause the yaw state to drift over time.
criteria.rationale: The stated acceptance criterion rules out claiming absolute yaw from accelerometer correction and explicitly allows Z-orientation drift. Inspecting the yaw update checks both points without treating the permitted drift as a failure.

criteria.criterion: The requirements and verification baseline assign no MPU6050 I²C address, calibration procedure, or orientation-filter parameter value as a PRD-specified value.
criteria.observable: The MPU6050 address, calibration, and filter-parameter statements in the requirements and verification baseline
procedure: Inspect the requirements and verification baseline for MPU6050 I²C address assumptions.
Inspect them for a mandated sensor calibration procedure.
Inspect them for mandated orientation-filter parameter values.
criteria.expected: None of the three items is specified as a value or procedure supplied by the PRD.

criteria.criterion: The MPU6050 initialization call occurs before the first MPU6050 sensor-data acquisition attempt.
criteria.observable: The ordered initialization and acquisition events recorded by fake MPU6050 I/O
preconditions: The initialization and measurement flow can be exercised with fake I²C I/O.
procedure: Run the MPU6050 startup and measurement flow with fake I²C I/O that records events.
Inspect the order of the initialization event and the first sensor-data acquisition event.
criteria.expected: The MPU6050 initialization event precedes the first sensor-data acquisition attempt.

criteria.criterion: The DHT22 initialization call occurs before the first temperature or humidity read attempt.
criteria.observable: The ordered initialization and measurement events recorded by fake DHT22 I/O
preconditions: The DHT22 initialization and measurement flow can be exercised with fake I/O.
procedure: Run the DHT22 startup and measurement flow with fake I/O that records events.

criteria.expected: The DHT22 initialization event precedes the first temperature and humidity read attempt.

criteria.criterion: The firmware obtains the Wi-Fi and Blynk credential values from configuration-secret inputs.
criteria.observable: The configuration-secret declarations and the firmware configuration references that supply Wi-Fi and Blynk credentials.
procedure: Inspect the project configuration and secret-input declarations.
Trace the Wi-Fi and Blynk credential configuration references to their inputs.
criteria.expected: Both Wi-Fi and Blynk credential values are supplied through configuration secrets.

criteria.criterion: No password or authentication-token value appears in the commits of the public source repository.
criteria.observable: The contents of the public repository's committed files and commit history.
preconditions: The public source repository and its commit history are available for inspection.
procedure: Inspect the public repository's committed files and commit history.
Check for committed password and authentication-token values.
criteria.expected: No password or authentication-token value appears in any inspected commit.

criteria.criterion: No actual credential value appears in a source file intended for sharing or version control.
criteria.observable: The contents of source files intended for sharing or version control.
procedure: Identify the source files intended for sharing or version control.
Inspect those files for actual Wi-Fi or Blynk credential values.
criteria.expected: No actual credential value appears in the inspected source files.

criteria.criterion: The measurement-loop iteration count increases after the network is disconnected.
criteria.observable: The measurement-loop iteration count, or an observable measurement event emitted by each loop iteration.
preconditions: The measurement loop is running and producing observable measurements.
The device is connected to the network.
procedure: Record the measurement-loop count or latest measurement event.
Disconnect the network while the device is running.
Check the count or measurement events again.
criteria.expected: At least one additional measurement-loop iteration is observed after the disconnection.

criteria.criterion: After connectivity is restored, the device reconnects and a subsequent measurement is received by Blynk.
criteria.observable: The device's connection state and the subsequent measurement recorded by Blynk.
preconditions: The device is running and publishing measurements before the interruption.
A network interruption occurs.
Network connectivity becomes available again.
procedure: Interrupt network connectivity and confirm that publishing is interrupted.
Restore network connectivity.
Observe the device reconnecting and check Blynk for a measurement published after reconnection.
criteria.expected: The device reconnects, and Blynk receives at least one measurement after connectivity is restored.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's statement says to reconnect and resume publishing when possible, and its postcondition says publishing resumes after reconnection. Observing a received post-reconnection measurement provides a concrete check of both recovery and resumed publishing; the at-least-one event is the minimum observable evidence of resumption.

criteria.criterion: The Blynk configuration defines Template ID `TMPL3VjCwAzY1` and template name `ESPInterface`.
criteria.observable: Blynk template ID and template name in the firmware configuration
procedure: Inspect the firmware's Blynk configuration.
criteria.expected: Template ID is `TMPL3VjCwAzY1` and template name is `ESPInterface`.

criteria.criterion: With the supplied configuration and available Wi-Fi, the firmware reaches the Blynk IoT connected state.
criteria.observable: Blynk connection state reported by the firmware on the ESP32-C3
preconditions: The supplied Blynk and Wi-Fi configuration is available.
The ESP32-C3 has access to the configured Wi-Fi network and Blynk IoT.
procedure: Load the supplied configuration onto the board.
Power the board and allow it to connect.
Read the firmware's Blynk connection state.
criteria.expected: The Blynk connection state is connected over Wi-Fi.

criteria.criterion: Each publishing cycle emits all eight sensor values to their assigned Blynk datastreams, and consecutive cycles begin 2000 ms apart.
criteria.observable: Recorded virtual-pin writes and their timestamps from the publisher's fake I/O callbacks
preconditions: The portable publishing logic is callable with fake sensor inputs, a fake clock, and a recording Blynk I/O callback.
procedure: Provide eight distinct sensor values to the publisher.
Run the publisher for at least two cycles while advancing the fake clock.
Inspect the recorded writes and cycle timestamps.
criteria.expected: Each cycle records one write for each assigned datastream V0–V7, and consecutive cycle start timestamps differ by 2000 ms.

criteria.criterion: During normal operation, consecutive sensor-sampling events and consecutive publishing cycles each occur 2000 ms apart.
criteria.observable: Timestamps of sample and publish callbacks recorded by a fake-clock unit test
preconditions: The normal-operation loop is callable with a fake clock and recording sample and publish callbacks.
procedure: Run the normal-operation loop for at least three sampling and publishing events while advancing the fake clock.
Record the timestamps of each sample and publish callback.
Compare consecutive timestamps within each event sequence.
criteria.expected: Every pair of consecutive sample timestamps differs by 2000 ms, and every pair of consecutive publishing-cycle timestamps differs by 2000 ms.

criteria.criterion: The firmware's Blynk code writes values to the existing datastreams and contains no operation that creates a dashboard.
criteria.observable: Blynk write operations and dashboard-creation operations in the firmware source
preconditions: The existing dashboard and datastreams are available for reference.
procedure: Inspect the firmware's Blynk integration code.
Identify the operations that send values to datastreams.
Check whether the firmware contains an operation that creates a dashboard.
criteria.expected: The code sends values to the existing datastreams, and no dashboard-creation operation is present.
